title: Ironshore claims prompt iteration notes
notes:
Call notes (2026-02-18) - Ironshore claims automation sync with CS + SE

Attendees: Nadia Park (Redwood), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Evelyn Brooks (Customer PM - Ironshore Claims), Samir Patel (Customer Data Eng), Luis Gomez (Ironshore SME)

High level objective:
- Build a proof-of-concept that classifies incoming claim submissions into 6 disposition buckets and extracts 3 structured fields (policy_id, incident_date, claimant_role).
- Keep latency < 200ms p50 for single request path, and p95 < 450ms for batched inference at Ironshore pilot traffic (expected avg 25 rps, burst 120 rps).

Key requirements captured:
- 6 disposition labels: duplicate, fraud-suspect, requires-docs, high-severity, low-severity, triage-manual
- Confidence threshold configurable per label (customer wants automatic routing only for high-confidence classifications)
- Field extraction must preserve original casing and return offsets for downstream redaction pipeline
- All data must stay within Ironshore VPC; Redwood Private deployment with KMS integration
- Audit log for every inference (prompt, model_id, latency, decision, confidence) stored for 90 days

Customer constraints / gotchas they emphasized:
- Their claims text often contains scanned OCR noise: LOTS of weird spacing/newline fragments and poor dates ("03/02" ambiguous). Need robust date normalization and fuzzy matching for policy IDs (they have multiple legacy ID formats).
- They will not accept any external calls during triage — no webhooks to external validation endpoints in pilot.
- Small minority of claims include PHI-ish text; legal wants redaction hooks before any logs leave the VPC (we must ensure the audit log is stored to their S3 and not sent to Redwood-hosted services).
- Existing rules engine will handle clear duplicates; model should flag probable duplicates but not auto-close unless confidence > 0.98

Model/Prompting specifics discussed:
- Start with a two-step approach: 1) classification prompt (zero-shot/shot few), 2) structured extraction prompt for fields. Evaluate merging into single-call structured output if latency/units favorable.
- Use schema-checking wrapper: require JSON schema output and validate on edge. If schema mismatch, fallback to safe-route (manual triage).
- Provide examples (10+) from their backlog for few-shot tuning; they agreed to provide 300 labeled examples by next week for in-house finetune/adapter testing.

Evaluation & acceptance criteria:
- Accuracy: macro-F1 >= 0.88 across labels on held-out set (they will supply 2k holdout).
- Field extraction: exact match for policy_id >= 0.95, date extraction tolerance +/- 1 day on normalized dates for 0.92 of cases.
- Latency: single-shot p50 < 200ms, p95 < 350ms on dedicated pilot cluster.
- No audit data leaves VPC; integration tested end-to-end.

Operational notes / seams:
- Batching: run continuous-batching with max latency budget 80ms (target) for batching window; need per-customer priority token to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- KV cache: useful for repeated follow-ups (claimant asking clarifying Qs); propose caching last inference per claim_id for 10 minutes.
- Canary rollouts: start 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on accuracy regression or error-rate > 2.5%.

Open questions / blockers (action items inline):
- (EVELYN) Confirm allowed storage location and S3 prefix for audit logs. [Due 2026-02-22]
- (SAMIR) Provide sample of 300 labeled examples and 2k holdout set. Also share schema for legacy policy IDs. [Due 2026-02-25]
- (NADIA) Validate whether Ironshore legal accepts temporary logging to Redwood for dev testing (they indicated no, but check for dev sandbox exception). [Due 2026-02-20] - NOTE: customer initially said NO, but want to confirm sandbox path.
- (MARCO) Prototype prompt templates and send 3 variants (concise, instructive, schema-strong) and rough token-cost estimate. [Due 2026-02-24]
- (NADIA) Prepare Private deployment checklist (KMS, VPC peering, S3 policies, audit retention). [Due 2026-02-23]
- (TEAM) Decide on few-shot vs light adapter fine-tune tradeoffs after we see the 300 examples. Cost estimate for adapter vs hosted few-shot needs to be prepared. [Discussion 2026-02-26]

Short-term next steps (this sprint):
1) Send prompt variations + small eval harness (Marco) — include unit tests for schema mismatch fallback.
2) Customer to drop 300 tagged examples + holdout details (Samir/Evelyn).
3) SE to stand up private dev cluster dummy (no PHI) for integration smoke tests (Nadia/Infra).
4) Legal sync to confirm redaction hook + sandbox rules (Nadia).

Longer-term roadmap items (not blockers for pilot):
- Adapter-based finetune if few-shot not meeting accuracy after 2 iterations.
- Integrate deterministic policy-id lookup via fast index (embed+ANN) for higher precision on policy mapping.
- Auto-escalation workflow for claims flagged as fraud-suspect: wire to fraud team queue + attach evidence.

Notes-to-self (raw):
- Watch out for date formats in OCR: build a date-preprocessor that leverages context (e.g., if incident_date in future vs past).
- Consider tokenization quirks: heavy punctuation/noise -> use cleaning before prompt; but keep raw text for extraction offsets mapping (store mapping table).
- For audit log schema, include: request_id, claim_id, model_id, prompt_version, output_schema_version, latency_ms, confidence_scores, routing_decision, timestamp.

Meeting follow-up planned: 2026-02-25 (tech deep-dive) — schedule provisional 60m with Ironshore eng, send calendar invite after Samir confirms sample delivery.

This doc is intentionally informal — iterative record while building pilot. Will curate into a neat one-pager for exec summary once the sample data lands and we have initial eval numbers.
